correctness.rationale: For every n>=1 the reflexive path modal pair is bijective with ternary output words of the boundary-repeated three-bit transducer. Its determinization has the twelve explicitly tabulated reachable states. The polynomial numerators P_0,...,P_11 satisfy all twelve exact transfer equations with denominator 1-z-z^2-z^3, giving a proof for all n of the rational generating function, Tribonacci recurrence for n>=5, and its dominant-pole asymptotic. The self-contained standard-library verifier independently rebuilds the transition table, checks all polynomial identities, and exhaustively enumerates direct approximation pairs for n<=15; it returned VERIFY_OK. Finite checks alone are not used to infer the infinite statement.

originality.rationale: 2022 rough-set semantic framework and 2015 preclusivity path/cycle analysis do not supply the same-reflexive-tolerance joint image cardinality in their materially inspected results. The 2015 similarity relation is the complement of irreflexive graph adjacency rather than the present reflexive adjacency. The 2018/2019 tolerance-compatible equivalence paper counts pairs built from two different relations. A related Tribonacci fan-graph dissociation result has distinct counted objects and initial terms. The accessible published mathematical results and prior scientific claims showed no covering claim; no exhaustive originality certification is asserted.

value.rationale: Counting distinct joint certainty/possibility profiles rather than raw valuations or one modal coordinate measures the semantic information retained by tolerance approximations. A reflexive path is the simplest non-equivalence connected sparse tolerance frame, and the exact growth law for all path lengths is mathematically motivated. The twelve-state automaton gives a global structural explanation, the rational series and Tribonacci recurrence solve the infinite census, and the asymptotic growth constant sharply quantifies an exponential information-collapse rate. This exact natural invariant is useful without needing a claimed downstream theorem. Generalizing to arbitrary graphs and fiber multiplicities remains open here.
